body.statement: Can \(\mathsf{Purify}_R\) be realized so that, for every \(c\in\mathcal C_R\), its output \(c'\in\mathcal U_R\) satisfies \(2N_{c'}\ge2N_c\) and \(f_{c'}(n_B,n_S)\ge f_c(n_B,n_S)\) simultaneously for all \(n_B,n_S\ge4R\), with equality conditions tracked in both directions?
body.justification: A positive answer would replace the certified finite catalog computation by a smaller diagonal unit-residual search and could expose a closed all-resolution extremal mechanism, but it is not needed for the proved affine frontier.
body.gap: Neither the support-preserving residual-copy comparison nor a one-dimensional LYM/unit-rank reduction realizes the required elementary compression while preserving the chosen common bivariate fiber. Simultaneous support dominance, affine-score dominance for all admissible aspect ratios, and the equality cases therefore remain unproved.
body.consumer: Designers can already compute the exact optimum by finite catalog enumeration. Resolving this question would simplify that computation further, but no current implementation or validity claim depends on it.

obligation.what_is_open: A common-fiber-preserving realization of the purification program that maps every residual catalog entry to a diagonal unit-residual entry while weakly increasing both common support and affine score at every admissible pair of margins, together with a two-way equality characterization.
obligation.obstruction: The available pure-profile reduction is one-dimensional and does not preserve a prescribed joint buyer--seller subset-sum fiber. The residual-copy comparison used by optimizer containment preserves the relevant support only while replacing one side by a copy of the other side's residual coordinates; it does not split arbitrary paired residual coordinates into diagonal unit coordinates. Consequently it supplies neither the required universal map into \(\mathcal U_R\) nor the score comparison and equality conditions for all \(n_B,n_S\ge 4R\).
obligation.attempted: The support-preserving residual-copy route and the proposed LYM/unit-rank route were compared with the stated purification handle. The former proves finite residual concentration but does not perform the required unit-coordinate elementary compressions. The latter controls ranks in a single subset-sum poset but does not control the intersection of the two weighted target fibers, so its injections need not preserve the common bivariate fiber. Neither route yields the simultaneous inequalities or their equality cases.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved catalog machinery supplies a finite, computable substitute for the unresolved purification.  Specifically, \(\textnormal{thm:affine-frontier}\) gives, for every \(R\ge 4\) and \(n_B,n_S\ge 4R\),
\[
\Phi_{n_B,n_S}(R)=\max_{c\in\mathcal C_R} f_c(n_B,n_S).
\]
It also identifies the optimizing profiles with the catalog argmax profiles, modulo common block permutation and simultaneous complementation, and records every tie through the affine phase inequalities.  The set \(\mathcal C_R\) is finite: its definition bounds \(m,A,D\) by \(2R\), positivity leaves only finitely many integer vectors \(u,v\), and \(p\in\{0,\ldots,A\}\), \(q\in\{0,\ldots,D\}\).  Thus both the frontier and all catalog equality cases are exactly enumerable for each fixed \(R\).  This result neither constructs a map from \(\mathcal C_R\) to \(\mathcal U_R\) nor proves simultaneous support and score dominance by a unit-residual entry.
